name: Jiang Weihai
current_role: Co-founder, former director and general manager, Henan Xindaxin Materials (Kaifeng); current role not found
profile: Senior engineer who co-founded Henan Xindaxin Materials, a Kaifeng maker of silicon-carbide slicing powders used to cut solar-grade silicon wafers. Second-largest shareholder (22.56%) and GM at its 2010 ChiNext IPO (300080). The company was later taken over by state-owned Pingmei Shenma and renamed Yicheng New Energy; his current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: Xindaxin's core product was specialised silicon-carbide 'edge material' (刃料) for slicing crystalline-silicon solar wafers; Jiang personally co-developed the dedicated solar-cell wafer-slicing powder project in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: Started in 1982 as a technician at China No.2 Grinding Wheel Factory, served as deputy township head of Yingyang, Dengfeng (1991-93), then ran Zhengzhou White Dove Micro-powder and worked on 20+ White Dove Group R&D projects before joining Xindaxin in 2004.
notes: Hurun 2010 listing. Born Dec 1962 per IPO prospectus. No current public profile or contacts found; Yicheng New Energy (300080.SZ) is now state-controlled, so the old company is not a route to him. MarketScreener lists a 'Wei Hai Jiang' but match unverified.

name: Uday J Desai
current_role: Founder director / managing director, Frost International Ltd (Mumbai commodity trader) per company registry listings
profile: Uday Jayant Desai is listed as founder director and managing director of Frost International Ltd, a Mumbai commodity-trading company (incorporated 1995, also with a Kanpur presence) that traded a large portfolio of agri and other commodities. Hurun ranked him in 2017-18. Registry sites show the company under insolvency resolution (CIRP) as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Frost International traded a broad commodity portfolio out of Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex and Kanpur; company material credits Uday J. Desai as founder director who grew its trade volumes.

name: Mahendra Nahata
current_role: Promoter & Managing Director, HFCL Ltd; director, Reliance Jio Infocomm
profile: Kolkata-raised B.Com (St. Xavier's) who co-promoted Himachal Futuristic Communications (HFCL) in 1987, building it from transmission equipment into a telecom gear, optical-fibre and defence-electronics maker. MD since 2005 and on the Jio Infocomm board; in 2026 he is pushing HFCL's record order book and calling for Indian data-centre and R&D expansion.
interesting_fact: Voice & Data named him 'Telecom Man of the Millennium' in 2003; he also has been president of the Telecom Equipment Manufacturers Association of India, and his family holds a stake in Jio Platforms.
deep_cut_fact: Before telecom, he began his business career dabbling in tea trading out of New Jalpaiguri, a small town in north Bengal.
notes: Strong podcast fit: publicly advocating data-centre and telecom-infrastructure build-out (Entrepreneur India 2026: https://india.entrepreneur.com/business-news/entrepreneur-2026-hfcls-mahendra-nahata-calls-for-infra-data-centre-expansion-and-rd-investment). Son Anant Nahata runs Exicom (EV chargers/telecom power). Route via HFCL company secretary/IR.

name: Hu Jishen
current_role: Chairman of the board, Xingyue Group (Yongkang, Zhejiang) per brand-profile site; date unverified
profile: Founder figure of Xingyue (Star Moon) Group in Yongkang, Zhejiang, which grew from a small workshop into a diversified manufacturer of power equipment/engines, doors and tools, reportedly with 4,000+ staff and a place among China's top 500 private firms. Hurun listed him (with Hu Jirong) in 2005-07. Current activity not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Xingyue grew from a factory with annual output under RMB 1 million into a group with over RMB 2 billion in assets, spanning engines, doors and hardware tools in Yongkang, China's 'hardware capital'.
deep_cut_fact: He served about 20 years as Party secretary of Gushan village in Gushan town, Yongkang, and reportedly put around RMB 30 million into the village's infrastructure; he was also vice-chair of the Jinhua federation of industry and commerce.
notes: Only source is a promotional brand-directory profile (CNPP); verify before use. Shares the Hurun listing with Hu Jirong (relationship not confirmed). No published contacts found.

name: Gerold Buettiker
current_role: Chairman, Gebuka AG (Swiss investment company); ~13% holder of Aebi Schmidt Holding AG (Nasdaq: AEBI)
profile: Swiss industrialist/investor (ETH, University of Zurich doctorate) holding his Aebi Schmidt stake via wholly owned Gebuka AG. He sat on Aebi Schmidt's supervisory board before its 2025 merger with The Shyft Group and Nasdaq listing, and has held board seats at Swiss Steel, Deutsche Edelstahlwerke and Nueva Holding.
interesting_fact: After Aebi Schmidt merged with US truck-body maker Shyft Group in 2025 and listed on Nasdaq, Büttiker emerged as one of its two major shareholders with about 13%.
notes: Very low public profile; stake held via Gebuka AG (Neuheim, Switzerland) per Schedule 13G https://www.secform4.com/13dg/2081403/0001214659-25-012273.html. Board roles from MarketScreener aggregator. No published personal/office contact; Aebi Schmidt IR would be the only corporate route.

name: C Sathyan
current_role: Vice Chairman, Hatsun Agro Product Ltd (Chennai)
profile: Son of founder R.G. Chandramogan, C. (Chandramogan) Sathyan became executive director of Hatsun Agro in 2002, later MD and since 2024 (Executive) Vice Chairman, supporting the chairman on strategy. Hatsun is India's largest private dairy (Arun Ice Creams, Arokya milk, Hatsun curd, Ibaco), buying milk from 400,000+ farmers across South India.
interesting_fact: Hatsun began in 1970 as a single Arun ice-cream shed in Chennai started with Rs 13,000 and now procures millions of litres of milk a day; it famously earns more in minutes today than in its first decade.
notes: Signed filings as Vice Chairman in March 2026, so active. Little personal press; father R.G. Chandramogan is the public face. Best route is Hatsun's corporate office.

name: Rudra Chatterjee
current_role: Managing Director, Luxmi Group (Luxmi Tea / Luxmi Estates); Chairman, Obeetee Carpets; Chairman, Silverback Tea
profile: Kolkata businessman who has run century-old Luxmi Tea (MD since 2007), producing ~30 million kg of tea from about 25 estates in India and Africa and owning the Makaibari Darjeeling brand. He also chairs Obeetee, India's historic hand-knotted carpet maker, and is pushing Luxmi (rebranded Luxmi Estates) into global direct-to-consumer tea.
interesting_fact: Under him Makaibari made a special-edition tea for King Charles III's coronation and hosted a G20 event at the estate, while Obeetee supplied carpets for India's new Parliament building and Rashtrapati Bhavan.
deep_cut_fact: Asked about the big projects, he deflected credit: he said he may be part of it but is not all of it - many other members are pulling it.
notes: Media-friendly: speaks at tea conventions and gives interviews (Telegraph t2, tea-biz). Route via Luxmi Estates / Makaibari corporate comms; no published email found in this pass.

name: Douglas Valenti
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, QuinStreet Inc. (Nasdaq: QNST), Foster City, CA
profile: Founded performance-marketing firm QuinStreet in 1999 (CEO since 1999, chairman since 2004) and took it public in 2010; it runs online customer-acquisition marketplaces for insurance, financial and home services. Georgia Tech industrial engineer, Stanford MBA, ex-Rosewood Capital partner and McKinsey consultant. Owns ~3.4% of QNST.
interesting_fact: Before founding QuinStreet he worked at McKinsey, Procter & Gamble and venture firm Rosewood Capital, and graduated from Georgia Tech in industrial engineering with highest honors.
deep_cut_fact: He spent five years as a U.S. Navy nuclear submarine officer before going into business school and consulting.
notes: IR contact (Robert Amparo) is the published route. Low personal media profile beyond earnings calls.

name: Brad Marshall
current_role: Global Head of Private Credit Strategies, Blackstone; Chairman & CEO of Blackstone Private Credit Fund (BCRED) and Blackstone Secured Lending (BXSL)
profile: New York-based Blackstone Senior Managing Director who joined in 2005 and built its direct-lending franchise; he chairs and leads BCRED and BXSL, two of the largest private-credit vehicles, and sits on the private credit investment committee. Earlier at RBC (fixed income research, PE funds) and CIBC's TAL Global; Queen's University economics and McGill MBA.

deep_cut_fact: Before finance at Blackstone, he co-founded a microchip verification software company where he served as CFO.
notes: Route via Blackstone media relations (press contacts on blackstone.com; site blocked automated fetch so no email verified). Private credit is a major financier of digital infrastructure - relevant to the podcast theme.

name: John W Casella
current_role: Executive Chairman, Casella Waste Systems (Nasdaq: CWST), Rutland, Vermont (CEO until end-2025)
profile: Co-built Casella Waste Systems from his brother Doug's one-truck hauling business started in Rutland, Vermont in 1975 into a Nasdaq-listed waste, recycling and resource-management company across the Northeast. Director since 1993, chairman since 2001 and long-time CEO; Executive Chairman since January 2026 (Ned Coletta now CEO).
interesting_fact: Casella marked its 50th anniversary in 2025; the business began when Doug Casella used his high-school savings to buy a truck and collect trash around Killington, with John handling administration and permits.
deep_cut_fact: Before trash, John worked in the hospitality industry like his parents; he helped with paperwork part-time and only became Doug's full-time partner about a year after the 1975 start. The brothers also founded Casella Construction in 1987.
notes: Media route: Jeff Weld, VP Communications (phone published in press releases). Has advised governors of VT, NY and NH on solid-waste policy (aggregator profile). Casella runs landfill-gas/renewable-energy projects - possible energy-podcast angle.

name: S. Matthew Schultz
current_role: Co-founder, CEO & Chairman, CleanSpark Inc. (Nasdaq: CLSK)
profile: Utah-based financier turned energy entrepreneur who co-founded CleanSpark, steering it from biomass power and microgrid software into one of North America's largest bitcoin miners and now an AI data-center developer. CEO 2014-19, then executive chairman, he returned as CEO in August 2025; he says he has helped raise over $3.8bn in capital.
interesting_fact: CleanSpark began as an alternative-energy company converting biomass into power with a patented gasifier, then built microgrid software deployed notably at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, before pivoting to bitcoin mining and AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before CleanSpark he chaired Pali Financial Group (1999-2003), helping early-stage public companies raise capital, and was a founding member and former vice president of the Utah Consumer Lending Association.
notes: Top podcast fit (energy + bitcoin mining + AI data centers). Frequent conference/podcast speaker (Blockworks events). Deep-cut sourced from aggregator bio (insidertrades) - cross-check with CleanSpark proxy. LinkedIn listed is the company page, not personal.

name: Ramesh Srinivasan
current_role: President & CEO, Agilysys Inc. (Nasdaq: AGYS)
profile: Has led hospitality-software firm Agilysys since January 2017, shifting it to cloud/subscription products for hotels, resorts, casinos and cruise lines with a long run of record revenue quarters. Previously CEO of Bally Technologies (2012-14), Innotrac and Ooyala, and a warehouse-management software leader at Manhattan Associates.
interesting_fact: Under him Agilysys posted 17 consecutive record-revenue quarters through fiscal 2026, reaching record annual revenue of about $319m with subscription revenue growing ~30%.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer at IIT (Banaras Hindu University), Varanasi, took his MBA at IIM Bangalore, and spent 1998-2005 at Manhattan Associates, ending as EVP of Warehouse Management Systems, before running Bally's systems business.
notes: IR contact Jessica Hennessy (VP IR) named on releases. Regular earnings-call speaker; hospitality-tech rather than energy, so weaker podcast fit.

Earlier he was CEO of PENSCO Trust (self-directed IRAs, 2010-16) and briefly ran wealth services at Opus Bank.

profile: Stockholm private-equity veteran on EQT's founding team in 1994 and its CEO/Managing Partner 2014-2019, ahead of the 2019 IPO. name: Christopher David Young
current_role: President & CEO, Vertex Inc. (Nasdaq: VERX) since Nov 2025; director, Qualcomm and American Express
profile: Cybersecurity and tech executive who ran McAfee as CEO (2017-20), leading its spin-out from Intel, then served as Microsoft's EVP of Business Development, Strategy and Ventures (2020-25), reporting to Satya Nadella. He became CEO of tax-technology firm Vertex in November 2025 and sits on the Qualcomm and American Express boards.

notes: High-profile, media-experienced exec (CNBC appearances as McAfee CEO). Qualcomm board seat is relevant to AI/data-center themes. Route via Vertex PR.

name: Christopher A. Kroeger
current_role: Founder, CEO & Director, MapLight Therapeutics (Nasdaq: MPLT)
profile: Physician-entrepreneur who founded MapLight (with Stanford's Karl Deisseroth and Robert Malenka) to develop CNS drugs; it IPO'd on Nasdaq in October 2025, raising ~$296m, with lead drug ML-007C-MA in Phase 2 for schizophrenia and Alzheimer's psychosis. Previously CEO of Cardioxyl (sold to Bristol Myers Squibb for up to $2.1bn) and of OvaScience.
interesting_fact: MapLight's scientific founders include Karl Deisseroth, the Stanford pioneer of optogenetics, whose circuit-mapping approach underpins the company's platform.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a surgeon: Harvard biology BA, Stanford MD, general-surgery residency at Brigham and Women's Hospital, then an HBS MBA, before becoming a VC partner at The Aurora Funds.
notes: Biotech, not energy - weaker podcast fit but a strong founder story (two prior exits). Also on boards of Stellaromics and Antlia Biosciences.

name: Timothy J Naughton
current_role: Chair, Vivmark Residential (NYSE: VMRK; AvalonBay's successor company); director, BXP Inc. and Park Hotels & Resorts
profile: Apartment-REIT veteran who joined AvalonBay's predecessor in 1989 and rose through development to President (2005), CEO (2012-2022) and Chairman (since 2013), building one of the largest US multifamily REITs. He now chairs Vivmark Residential (led by CEO Ben Schall), sits on the BXP and Park Hotels boards, and is a former Nareit chairman.
interesting_fact: He led AvalonBay as CEO for a decade and remained its chair into its next chapter as Vivmark, a ~184,000-home rental-housing company.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Virginia graduate elected to Phi Beta Kappa (Class of '83), he took his Harvard MBA in 1987 and joined AvalonBay's predecessor in 1989 in the middle of a real-estate recession.
notes: Vivmark appears to be the renamed/merged AvalonBay (same CEO/CFO, all-stock merger) - verify exact corporate history before outreach. Active in ULI and Nareit; route via Vivmark/AvalonBay IR.

profile: Finance executive who has been CFO of Casey's, the Midwest convenience-store and fuel chain, since May 2020, overseeing finance, fuel, strategy, M&A and data/analytics.
